note: The OLG covers several elements of the FNS negative allegation investigation protocol but does not present them as a unified, systematic procedure for when a household denies employment. Specifically: (1) Work Number/wage match checks are well-covered — BEACON automatically checks Work Number at recertification and IR, and the OLG has detailed procedures for resolving matches (Simplified Reporting – Interim Report, Simplified Reporting – Recertification, The Work Number). (2) SLAM procedures (Addressing SLAM) require workers to explore how expenses are being met when they exceed income, partially covering FNS's requirement to investigate when shelter costs exceed reported income. (3) Collateral contact is documented as a verification method (Collateral Contact page) with procedures for when and how to use it, but it is framed as an alternative when documentary evidence is unavailable — not as a proactive investigative tool for exploring denied employment. (4) The Case Accuracy Assistant flags cases with 'dependent care expenses with no income' for follow-up, covering one suspicious-situation indicator. However, the OLG lacks: (a) a dedicated negative allegation protocol — no single procedure tells workers what to do when a household denies all employment; (b) explicit guidance to explore past employment history, types of work, and former employers; (c) instructions to investigate behavioral indicators of possible employment (member frequently absent, leaves at same time daily); (d) seasonal employment area investigation guidance; (e) procedures for verifying termination dates and final pay for known past employment; (f) explicit IEVS match procedures in the context of denied employment (the Work Number is covered but broader IEVS data matching for employment verification is not proceduralized for caseworkers). The OLG's coverage is fragmented across SLAM, Work Number, collateral contact, and IR procedures rather than consolidated into a negative allegation investigation workflow.
